title: Basic English — Course 1, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 07

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Listen to Oliver's message. Where will the project group meet?
tasks.audioText: Hi, Oliver. Our project group is meeting in the media room tomorrow. The room is free from two until three thirty. Please bring the pictures you found and your notes. I will bring my laptop. We need to choose three pictures for the college website and write short captions. If you cannot come, send your ideas to the group chat before lunch.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. What should a student do if they cannot attend the meeting?
tasks.audioText: Hi, Oliver. Our project group is meeting in the media room tomorrow. The room is free from two until three thirty. Please bring the pictures you found and your notes. I will bring my laptop. We need to choose three pictures for the college website and write short captions. If you cannot come, send your ideas to the group chat before lunch.
options: Send ideas to the group chat before lunch
Ask the teacher to cancel the project

tasks.prompt: Reading 1. Read the text. Last month, Irina helped at the college open day. She welcomed visitors at the entrance and showed them where to find the workshops. She also gave out maps and answered simple questions about the timetable. Irina was tired at the end of the day, but she enjoyed meeting new people. Next year, she wants to help organise the event. What did Irina give to visitors?
Reading 2. What does Irina want to do next year?
Choose the correct Past Simple form: 'Yesterday our group ___ a short presentation.'
Select TWO grammatically correct questions in the Past Simple.
options: Did she helped at the open day?

tasks.prompt: Complete the sentence with one word: 'A person who works to help others without receiving money is a ___.'
You cannot attend a group meeting. Which message is the most appropriate?
options: I'm sorry, I can't attend the meeting. I'll send my ideas before lunch.

tasks.prompt: Put the steps for preparing a short group presentation in a logical order.
options: Choose the topic and main points
correctOrder: Choose the topic and main points

tasks.prompt: Write 60–80 words about a college event or group project you took part in, or would like to take part in. Explain what students do, what your role is and why teamwork is useful.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the event or project is identified and the student's role is explained (0–2); the response describes what students do and gives a relevant reason teamwork is useful (0–2); basic grammar and sentence links are understandable (0–2); event/teamwork vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
